facts.statement: Archaeoceratops was a small, bipedal dinosaur reaching 0.9 meters in length and 10 kilograms in body mass.
facts.quote: It appears to have been bipedal and quite small, reaching 0.9 m in length and 10 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Archaeoceratops had a large head with no horns, only a small bony frill at the back of its skull.
facts.quote: It had a comparatively large head but no horns, possessing only a small bony frill projecting from the back of its head.

facts.statement: Fossils of Archaeoceratops were found in the Gongpoquan Basin of Gansu Province, north central China.
facts.quote: Two specimens were found in the Middle Gray Unit of the Xinminbao Group, Gongpoquan Basin of the Mazong Shan area of Gansu Province, north central China.

facts.statement: The type species Archaeoceratops oshimai was named by Dong Zhiming and Azuma in 1997.
facts.quote: The type species, A. oshimai, was named by Dong Zhiming and Azuma in 1997.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of this small dinosaur was found in 1992 in the Xinminbao Group of the Gongpoquan Basin in Gansu Province, China.
facts.quote: Un esqueleto parcial de este pequeño dinosaurio fue hallado en 1992 en el Grupo Xinminbao de la Cuenca Gongpoquan de Mazong Shan Gansu, provincia de China.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was named by Dong and Azuma in 1996.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado por Dong y Azuma en 1996.

facts.statement: In 1997, Dong and Azuma placed Archaeoceratops in the new family Archaeoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: In 1997 Dong and Azuma placed it in a new family, Archaeoceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Archaeoceratops lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 140 to 130 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 140 y 130 millones de años, desde el Valanginiense hasta el Hauteriviense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Archaeoceratops was a herbivore, like all ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Archaeoceratops, like all ceratopsians, was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Because flowering plants were geographically limited during the Cretaceous, Archaeoceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: During the Cretaceous, flowering plants were "geographically limited on the landscape", and so it is likely that this dinosaur fed on the predominant plants of the era: ferns, cycads and conifers.

facts.statement: Archaeoceratops was a primitive ceratopsian that could adopt both bipedal and quadrupedal stances, had a small beak and frill, and a light body adapted for fast walking.
facts.quote: El arqueocerátopo era un ceratópsido primitivo, aún no evolucionado, los pocos restos que se han encontrado demuestran que carecía de cuernos, que podía adoptar la configuración bípeda y cuadrúpeda, que su pico y gola eran pequeños y que su cuerpo era liviano, adaptado para caminar rápido.

facts.statement: While the exact size and weight are unknown, Archaeoceratops is estimated to have been about 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: Por ahora se desconoce exactamente su tamaño y peso, lo que es seguro es que fue algo pequeño, se estima que medía como 1 metro de longitud.

facts.statement: The species A. yujingziensis differs from others by some details of the jaw and teeth.
facts.quote: A. yujingziensis se diferencia por algunos detalles de la mandíbula y de los dientes.

rejected.quote: Archaeoceratops, meaning "ancient horned face", is a genus of basal neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) of north central China.
